content.title: Steel Tariffs Not Hurting U.S. Manufacturing, Nucor Chief Says
content.summary: Higher tariffs have been effective at driving imported steel out of the U.S. without damaging steel-consuming industries, Nucor Chief Executive Leon Topalian said.  Imports accounted for around 14% of the U.S. steel market in November, down from about 25% a year earlier, according to government and industry data.  “We’ve seen import levels I’ve never seen in my 30 years at Nucor,” Topalian told analysts during a conference call.

content.title: Palantir and 5 More Stocks That Might Catch Trump’s Attention—in a Good Way
content.summary: There is a change in the way the federal government operates that investors need to incorporate into their thinking. The White House often points out that Trump is a businessman and his second administration has demonstrated a willingness to do business directly with American companies.

content.title: USA Rare Earth Deal Adds to Trump Administration's Portfolio
content.summary: The Trump administration plans to take a stake in a rare-earth metal company as part of a proposed $1.6 billion funding deal.  USA Rare Earth has a mining project in Texas and plans to manufacture rare-earth magnets—needed for drones, wind turbines and other technology—in Oklahoma.  The deal is the administration’s latest move to bolster the position of the U.S. in critical industries.

content.title: Trump Administration Takes Stake in Critical Mineral Firm ATALCO
content.summary: The Defense Department and an affiliate of Pinnacle Asset Management are set to announce a strategic partnership Monday involving Atlantic Alumina Co., or ATALCO, which has been turning bauxite into alumina just outside of New Orleans since the late 1950s.  Alumina is a fine white powder used to make aluminum.
